LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts . Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot. The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline. Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Follow the game live here Where to watch Texans vs. Colts live Date: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: NRG Stadium (Houston) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Colts have the ball The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces. Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL . Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions. The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games. The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor 's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan , including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state. When the Texans have the ball C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season. The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner , either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins. It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. home.headline: Texans Have Two Offensive Injuries to Monitor After TNF Win
home.blurb: According to an update from the Texans during Thursday night's game, wide receiver Kayshon Boutte (hip) and offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge (stinger) would be deemed questionable for a return in the fourth quarter. We ultimately wound up seeing neither return to the action. But given that the Texans were so close to ending the game, it's unclear as to whether or not either player was dealing with a serious injury issue, or were simply being held out for precautionary reasons as the result of the game had already been decided. Rutledge was cleared to return on a short week against the Colts, but now after the same injury has surfaced once again, there might be a slim chance that Houston's first-round rookie is set to miss a little more time moving forward. As for Boutte, his hip injury seems to be a new issue to surface throughout Thursday night, which turned out to be a pretty successful night on his behalf. The Houston Texans put together a commanding win over the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night en route to a 26-3 victory that might just be the spark needed to help this team rattle off a few wins in a row through the second half of their season. However, in the midst of the Texans winning effort over the Colts, the team also saw their offense suffer a pair of injuries that will be worth keeping an eye on as they approach their next matchup. However, seeing both Boutte and Rutledge go down with an injury––each of whom has their respective key roles on the Texans' offense––is less than an ideal end to an overall successful night for Houston altogether. Kayshon Boutte, Keylan Rutledge Have Injuries to Keep Watch Of One of these injuries has been an issue the Texans have already seen surface earlier in the month, and that's the stinger that Rutledge suffered that makes for his second stinger in the past two weeks. The first stinger for Rutledge was bad enough that it led to him being sidelined for an entire week of the Texans' team practice , along with missing Week 10's game against the Cleveland Browns, forcing fourth-round rookie Febechi Nwaiwu into his first-ever start. Boutte converted on both of his targets against the Colts for two catches, 40 yards, and an aggressive touchdown reception in the second quarter for C.J. Stroud's second of three touchdown passes on the night––making for his second game on the season where he's seen over 40 yards in a single game. If Boutte is forced to miss any time, it'd mark yet another injury to the Texans’ wide receiver room following up on Jaylin Noel's injured reserve designation before Week 8 , along with the recent absence of Marvin Harrison Jr., which has led to him missing the last two games against the Browns and the Colts. away.headline: Dolphins get encouraging injury news on two receivers before Bills game
away.blurb: Miami’s passing game could have more help available Sunday as the Dolphins prepare for their AFC East matchup with the Buffalo Bills . Wide receivers Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell are expected to play, according to NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe. Miami Herald reporter Barry Jackson also reported Friday that head coach Jeff Hafley expects both receivers to be available. Douglas is dealing with a shoulder injury, while Bell has been working back from a knee injury that kept him out of Miami’s last game against the Indianapolis Colts. According to the Dolphins’ official injury report, both receivers were limited participants in practice Wednesday and Thursday, His expected return would give quarterback Kyle McCord another receiving option after Miami fell 24-22 at Indianapolis on Nov. 15. Bell’s return would add another option to a group that also received contributions from Malik Washington and Jalen Tolbert. Washington threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Tolbert on a trick play against the Colts, providing one of Miami’s biggest offensive moments. Having Douglas available and Bell back would give McCord more options as Miami tries to turn another competitive performance into a victory. The update offers good news for a receiving group that has dealt with multiple injuries throughout the week. Bell explained Thursday that he hyperextended his knee during practice last week. He did, however, express optimism about returning against Buffalo. “I think so. I hope so,” Bell said when asked whether he would play. Bell also expressed confidence that he still has more to show. “Nobody has seen the real Chris Bell yet,” he said. McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards and scored a rushing touchdown in his first NFL start. Douglas led the Dolphins with three catches for 71 yards, including a 38-yard reception that helped set up McCord’s late touchdown run. That production illustrates why Douglas’ expected availability matters. He snagged Miami’s longest reception against Indianapolis and helped create a scoring opportunity while the Dolphins were trying to erase a second-half deficit. The encouraging news does not resolve every concern at receiver, however. Jared Wayne missed Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices with a quadriceps injury, leaving another availability question for Miami to address. The Dolphins visit Buffalo on Sunday, Nov. 22, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m. ET. away.headline: Dolphins Final Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Trending Up, Trader Trending Down
away.blurb: Even though the Miami Dolphins listed center Aaron Brewer as questionable for their Week 11 game against the Buffalo Bills, all signs are pointing toward him being able to play Sunday. Brewer took the final step toward getting out of the concussion protocol when he took part in a full practice Friday, and the only hurdle remaining will be reporting no symptoms Saturday. The Dolphins did rule out two players Friday, punter Bradley Pinion and wide receiver Jared Wayne. The Dolphins listed two other players as doubtful, including starting safety Dante Trader Jr., but it's difficult to envision him playing after he didn't practice all week. Also listed as doubtful was cornerback Jaylin Simpson, who's dealing with a knee injury. He's mainly a special teams contributor and Baker might wind up taking his place. The best projection if Trader indeed is out against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Like the Dolphins, the Bills ruled out two players Friday and both happen to be starters on defense, cornerback Christian Benford and linebacker Dorian Williams The Bills also have injury issues at tight end, which could impact to some degree their running game. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

home.headline: Dolphins get encouraging injury news on two receivers before Bills game
home.blurb: Miami’s passing game could have more help available Sunday as the Dolphins prepare for their AFC East matchup with the Buffalo Bills . Wide receivers Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell are expected to play, according to NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe. Miami Herald reporter Barry Jackson also reported Friday that head coach Jeff Hafley expects both receivers to be available. Douglas is dealing with a shoulder injury, while Bell has been working back from a knee injury that kept him out of Miami’s last game against the Indianapolis Colts. According to the Dolphins’ official injury report, both receivers were limited participants in practice Wednesday and Thursday, His expected return would give quarterback Kyle McCord another receiving option after Miami fell 24-22 at Indianapolis on Nov. 15. Bell’s return would add another option to a group that also received contributions from Malik Washington and Jalen Tolbert. Washington threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Tolbert on a trick play against the Colts, providing one of Miami’s biggest offensive moments. Having Douglas available and Bell back would give McCord more options as Miami tries to turn another competitive performance into a victory. The update offers good news for a receiving group that has dealt with multiple injuries throughout the week. Bell explained Thursday that he hyperextended his knee during practice last week. He did, however, express optimism about returning against Buffalo. “I think so. I hope so,” Bell said when asked whether he would play. Bell also expressed confidence that he still has more to show. “Nobody has seen the real Chris Bell yet,” he said. McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards and scored a rushing touchdown in his first NFL start. Douglas led the Dolphins with three catches for 71 yards, including a 38-yard reception that helped set up McCord’s late touchdown run. That production illustrates why Douglas’ expected availability matters. He snagged Miami’s longest reception against Indianapolis and helped create a scoring opportunity while the Dolphins were trying to erase a second-half deficit. The encouraging news does not resolve every concern at receiver, however. Jared Wayne missed Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices with a quadriceps injury, leaving another availability question for Miami to address. The Dolphins visit Buffalo on Sunday, Nov. 22, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m. ET. picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions for New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears in Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football MLB trade targets Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended 4 Bold Predictions for New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears in Week 11 Neal Coolong · Athlon Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 6:06 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Soldier Field in late November isn't where a 3-6 team usually goes to turn its season around, but the New Orleans Saints are still one game behind Carolina in the NFC South. Carl Granderson and the Saints' pass rush get a 7-2 Chicago Bears team coming off its bye, with kickoff set for noon CT on FOX. New Orleans will be shorthanded up front. Center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga missed practice again Thursday, according to the Saints injury report , and Kellen Moore said Asim Richards will miss a few weeks with a knee injury. Here are four bold predictions for how the Saints pull the upset anyway. Carl Granderson and Chase Young combine for three sacks Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints defensive end Chase Young (99) reacts to a play against the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Granderson has 8.5 sacks and Young has eight, and the two of them have carried the pass rush all season. Against Carolina, Granderson had seven pressures and Young had five, according to PFF . Set that next to what Chicago has allowed. Caleb Williams has been sacked 14 times in six games, while the Saints' two edge rushers have 16.5 sacks between them. Chicago's Super Bowl hopes depend on Williams staying upright. Three sacks between Granderson and Young keep this a low-scoring game, which is the only kind New Orleans can win. Saints hold the Bears under 100 rushing yards Oct 19, 2025; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (4) runs the ball against New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (33) and linebacker Pete Werner (20) during the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images The Bears average 142 rushing yards per game. D'Andre Swift leads them with 576 yards and 10 touchdowns, and Kyle Monangai, a full participant this week after a toe injury, has averaged 5.4 yards per carry. New Orleans has been better against the run since its bye. Cleveland and Carolina combined for 192 yards on 66 carries, 2.9 per attempt, according to the Saints' team site . "From a big-picture perspective, felt like controlling their run game was important, I felt like we did that," Moore said Monday. Linebacker Pete Werner, who leads the team with 70 tackles, missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a hamstring injury, which makes this one bolder. Kaden Elliss had seven stops against Carolina, and he'll have to clean up the middle if Werner can't go. Jordyn Tyson catches his first NFL touchdown Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (0) dives for the sideline with Cleveland Browns cornerback Myles Harden (26) defending during the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn ImagesMatthew Hinton-Imagn Images The rookie has taken over Bryce Lance's snaps , and he has 15 catches for 110 yards in two games. When Carolina took away Chris Olave , Tyson became Tyler Shough's top target. He's still looking for his first touchdown, and he was limited Wednesday and Thursday with a chest injury. If he plays, the red zone is where it happens. New Orleans has scored touchdowns on 72.4% of its red-zone trips, and Chicago will spend plenty of attention on Olave. Saints intercept Caleb Williams twice Oct 11, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (7) steals the ball and runs it in for a touchdown against Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Tai Felton (13) during the second half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images New Orleans has four interceptions all season, which is what makes this one bold. Julian Blackmon and Martin Emerson Jr. have two apiece, and Emerson missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a concussion. Williams has thrown five interceptions in six games, and Bears quarterbacks have nine as a team. Chicago is minus-4 in turnover margin and New Orleans is minus-8, according to the Saints' game preview . Some Bears fans already see a trap game here. Two takeaways spring it, and the Saints leave Chicago at 4-6 with a 23-20 win. away.headline: New Orleans Saints injury report: Five ruled out; Tyson good to go
away.blurb: The Saints will be without five players Sunday at Soldier Field, and the list hits the offensive line and the secondary hardest. New Orleans ruled out center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), tackle Asim Richards (knee), cornerback Martin Emerson (concussion), and safety Justin Reid (personal matter). None of the five practiced at all this week, so none of these come as a surprise, and Reid’s personal matter is the technical term for him being released by the team. The offensive line losses stand out most. Three linemen are out, including McCoy and Fuaga, and that’s a lot of reshuffling up front against a Bears defense that sacked Baker Mayfield four times in its last game. The back end is banged up, too. With Emerson and Reid out, cornerback Decamerion Richardson (thigh) is questionable after being limited all week. Linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) is also questionable, even though he didn’t practice once after leaving the Carolina game. Questionable after three missed practices usually leans toward sitting, so I wouldn’t count on Werner. Either way, Caleb Williams should see a thinner coverage group than usual. The Saints did get some good news. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest) was upgraded to a full practice Friday after two limited days. Alvin Kamara practiced fully after a rest day Wednesday, and running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) fully participated all week. All three carry no game designation. Linebacker Isaiah Stalbird missed Friday’s practice for a personal matter but also has no designation. The New Orleans Saints submitted their final injury report of the week on Thursday ahead of their Week 11 contest with the Chicago Bears. away.headline: New Orleans Saints injury report: Tyson still limited, Kamara returns
away.blurb: Wednesday’s initial report listed seven non-participants and two limited participants, and today’s report saw only one player upgraded. Veteran running back Alvin Kamara participated in full today after being listed as out for non-injury-related/personal matters yesterday. Otherwise, it’s pretty much the same, with rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson still limited with a chest injury. Along with Tyson, cornerback Decamerio Richardson was limited with a thigh injury. The New Orleans Saints submitted their second injury report of the week on Thursday ahead of their Week 11 contest with the Chicago Bears. Cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) were non-participants on defense, along with multiple offensive line starters: center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), and Asim Richards (knee), who had been filling in for Fuaga. away.blurb: Panthers vs. Saints injury report: Is Jaelan Phillips making return? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Panthers vs. Saints injury report: Is Jaelan Phillips making return? The Carolina Panthers are in a divisional battle this week as they're set to face the New Orleans Saints. Ahead of the matchup, the status of Jaelan Phillips was in question as he's dealt with a hamstring injury for several weeks. The good news is that it looks like he'll be making his return to the field, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. "Panthers edge Jaelan Phillips, who has been out since mid-October with a hamstring injury, is expected to play today, source said. He's listed as questionable," Rapoport wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Phillips is listed as questionable against the Saints, but it looks like he'll be playing. He was a full participant in practice during the middle of the week, but was then limited the next day. That may have raised some concern for some, but the good news is that he'll be back on the field. With the return of Phillips, they should have a good chance of getting back on track, and it'll be an interesting matchup against the Saints, who also have three wins this season and are in second place in the division. One of the reasons is injuries, and they're slowly getting back healthy. They've lost their last three games, but the funny thing is that they're still leading the division with a 3-5 record. It's once again been a slugfest in the NFC South, and there's a chance that the winner of the division won't have to win more than eight games. home.headline: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears
home.blurb: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears Sheesh. The New Orleans Saints (3-6) shared a lengthy injury report ahead of Sunday's game with the Chicago Bears (7-2), with seven players not participating and two other limited to start the week. They'll need all hands on deck for a chance at upsetting one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Let's hope they can get it done. And let's start with the good news. Rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) returned to full practice reps on Wednesday after missing several games between that shoulder injury and a stint in concussion protocol. We haven't seen him since the rookie exited Week 9's game in Paris against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Donaldson has been a productive rusher for New Orleans on limited snaps (averaging 4.8 yards per carry and a team-high 64.7% success rate), and he was just starting to earn a bigger role after initially getting on the field as a short-yardage specialist. He competes hard in pass protection, too. How snaps could be divided between him, Travis Etienne Jr., Alvin Kamara (more on him in a minute), and Audric Estime remains to be seen. What about those seven players who didn't practice? We expected Kamara (not injury related) would get his usual rest day, which has been a pattern since he suffered a Week 5 back injury. He turned 31 this summer and has worn a lot of tread off his tires so it makes sense to give him a lighter workload during the week, especially if he's going to have a reduced role on game days. Kamara was only on the field last Sunday for 16 snaps but he scored two touchdowns. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) did not practice on Wednesday due to a personal matter, and head coach Kellen Moore was noncommittal when asked if Reid was expected back on Thursday. Stay tuned. Backup right tackle Asim Richards (knee) and a couple of defensive starters who got nicked up against the Carolina Panthers -- cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) -- were held out of practice. Additionally, starting right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) and center Erik McCoy (biceps) both did not practice, though Moore said "we'll see" if either of them can return to work later this week. Two other players were limited to start the week: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest), who you can read more about here ; and backup corner Decamerion Richardson (thigh). We'll be watching for updates on their status as the week continues. home.blurb: Saints QB Tyler Shough Gets Encouraging Injury Update Before Bears Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Saints QB Tyler Shough Gets Encouraging Injury Update Before Bears Game NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints looks to pass against the Carolina Panthers in the second quarter of a game at Caesars Superdome on November 15, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Wes Hale/Getty Images) Getty Erik C. Anderson · HEAVY Fri, November 20, 2026 at 3:03 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough appears to have taken an encouraging step in his recovery from a left hand injury that has bothered him for more than a month. Shough was spotted practicing without the protective glove he had been wearing on his injured hand, according to Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football, who reported the development on Thursday, November 19. "Tyler Shough is no longer wearing a glove on his left hand at practice," Underhill reported. It's a small change with potentially significant implications for the Saints quarterback, who has been playing through two reported broken bones in his non-throwing hand. While the absence of the glove does not necessarily mean Shough is fully healed, it represents an encouraging development ahead of New Orleans' November 22 matchup against the Chicago Bears. Tyler Shough's Broken Hand Has Affected Saints Offense Shough's injury first became a concern in early October, when the quarterback was seen with his left hand heavily wrapped during the Saints' game against the Minnesota Vikings. As Heavy previously reported , head coach Kellen Moore was questioned about the severity of the injury but initially stopped short of confirming whether Shough had suffered a fracture. ESPN's Adam Schefter subsequently reported on October 18 that Shough was playing through two broken bones in his left hand. The injury reportedly forced Shough to change how he handed off the football, using his right hand instead of his customary left. For a quarterback, that's more than an inconvenience. Handoffs require precise timing and ball placement, and changing the mechanics can complicate exchanges with running backs. The protective glove also became a regular part of Shough's game-day appearance. According to CBS Sports , citing Luke Johnson of The New Orleans Times-Picayune, Shough was still wearing the glove during warmups ahead of New Orleans' November 8 game against the Cleveland Browns. Less than two weeks later, that protection was absent from Thursday's practice. Whether Shough has returned to his normal handoff mechanics remains unclear. But no longer needing the glove in practice suggests the injury may be becoming less restrictive. Saints Get Encouraging Tyler Shough Update Before Bears

The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. The Bengals keep rolling. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. picks.headline: Staff Predictions for Titans vs. Cowboys: A Close Game Across the Board, But Split 2 Ways on the Result
picks.blurb: Last week, the Titans On SI staff predicted an unfortunate defeat at the hands of the Jacksonville Jaguars. That came to pass, but not without enough positive momentum for a few of us to change our tune this week. The Titans enter Dallas with just one win in nine tries, and as of now, the top pick in the 2027 draft. Every discussion around this team is double-edged; the future takes hold on the now for a team in the Titans' position. For Sunday's Week 11 matchup with the Cowboys, the staff are evenly divided. Here are our individual cases for the outcome: Isaiah: Titans 34, Cowboys 38 In recent weeks, the Tennessee Titans have produced positive trends that have me cautiously optimistic heading into Jerry’s World, especially with QB Cam Ward seeming to find his stride. However, the Titans’ defense has fallen apart. Across their last three matchups, Tennessee has allowed an average of 36 points per game, including back-to-back games of at least 40 points given up.Although the Cowboys’ defense hasn’t lived up to expectations, QB Dak Prescott has led Dallas to a top-five scoring offense with an average of nearly 29 points per game. Dallas has the offensive weapons to dominate an underwhelming Tennessee secondary. I anticipate even a herculean effort from ex-Cowboys RB Tony Pollard can’t undo the Titans’ defensive errors from another loss. Lane: Titans 30, Cowboys 27 The Titans are 1-8 coming off a 17-point loss, but I feel good about the team's chances this week. It helps that Dallas has one of the worst defenses in the league and just swapped their defensive play-callers right before this matchup. It also helps that Cam Ward is on a tear and will return his best pass-catcher on the road this week. Like the rest of the staff, I think it'll come down to the wire. Ultimately, if Tennessee is going to pull away, it will be because Robert Saleh's defense finally finds a way to reward the offense for improving on a weekly basis. Give me the Titans in their second victory of the season in Week 11. Shaun: Titans 33, Cowboys 37 This just feels like the type of game where the Cowboys end up laying an egg and all of the national sports shows spend the week making fun of them because of it.I expect the Titans’ talented young tandem of QB Cam Ward and WR Carnell Tate to make their presence felt throughout the contest as they play together for the first time in nearly a month. It also wouldn’t shock me if RB Tony Pollard ends up having a big day against his former team.But with the Titans’ defensive struggles being just as bad, if not worse than Dallas’, I think the Titans end up falling just short in a game that produces a lot of points by both teams. Dharya: Titans 27, Cowboys 24 Tennessee’s offense is finally gaining momentum, while Dallas’s defense is going in the opposite direction. If Brian Daboll’s unit can play efficient, mistake-free football, and Robert Saleh’s defense holds Dak Prescott and the dynamic Cowboys’ offense in check, the Titans should pick up their second win of the year. The Titans have all the ingredients for an upset here. We'll see if the team can finally put together a complete game and pull off the win. Will it lead to results on the field? After a tough defeat at the hands of the San Francisco 49ers, and a change at defensive play-caller , the Tennessee Titans head to AT&T Stadium to deliver the next test to the Cowboys' defense. Can they rebound under Mike Pettine? The Dallas Morning News ' columnists and beat writers gave their predictions below. Tim Cowlishaw The Titans may be headed for another top pick in the draft, but their offense is keeping them in games, averaging 27.2 points per game the last four. Expect explosive plays from Tony Pollard. Where are the Cowboys mentally after seeing yet another change on defense with Mike Pettine now sending in plays instead of Christian Parker? Cowboys' injury list was their friend the first half of the season but significant players are now missing time. Not the cakewalk the point spread suggests for Dallas. Titans 30, Cowboys 22 Change can cause a spark, no doubt. It's why it wouldn't be a surprise to see the Cowboys' defense have an immediate improvement with Mike Pettine calling plays, rather than defensive coordinator Christian Parker. I'm just not ready to believe yet. Just as the Cowboys lost to the lowly Cardinals and Buccaneers (at the time), I think there's a real chance they could lose to the one-win Titans, as well. Titans 31, Cowboys 27 The Cowboys changed defensive play-callers but the defensive players remain. They will continue to give up big plays and big points to a Titans offense that is better than some realize. But this game, and the Thanksgiving matchup against the Eagles, will determine the fate of the Cowboys' season. If there is any hope of digging out of the hole they've created, they must win these next two. That extra motivation will be just enough to carry the home team. Cowboys 30, Titans 28 Abraham Nudelstejer On paper, the Titans are a beatable opponent. Then again, the Buccaneers looked beatable. So did the Cardinals. For Cam Ward, this game presents a golden opportunity to remind everyone why he was the No. 1 overall pick in last year's draft. Facing a Dallas defense that has struggled throughout the season and already cost its coordinator his play-calling duties, Ward has a chance to deliver the best performance of his young career. As for the Cowboys, there is little evidence that a turnaround is imminent. Dallas is just 1-3 at home, has scored 123 points and allowed exactly the same number, all while its owner watches in astonishment. Titans 27, Cowboys 24 Kevin Sherrington Now that Christian Parker's no longer a target, attention turns back the head coach. Beating Tennessee offers only a temporary respite for a beleaguered staff. They're all just dead men walking. The only way they can save themselves is winning the division, then winning at least one playoff game. Nothing less will do, and even that's not enough. Cowboys 31, Titans 20 Calvin Watkins The Cowboys went through a tough week talking about the changes with Christian Parker's role. Now comes the game, and while the Titans' record shows they are terrible, there is some talent on the roster. Dallas has more talent and should have one of its easiest wins of the year. Titans' Overloaded Injury Report May Put an Upset Over Jaguars on Ice in Week 10
away.blurb: But what about Tate and four other major players missing the contest? That isn't even mentioning another questionable designation on, you guessed it, the offensive side of the ball. Robert Saleh's post-bye goal was for this team to come out swinging. On top of that laundry list, RB Tyjae Spears is once again questionable. Spears hasn't played since October 18, in the Titans' win over the Indianapolis Colts. Forgive our staff for entering tomorrow with a pessimistic mindset , but things simply aren't falling in a positive way for Tennessee. Of course, this doesn't negate the positive draft capital the team acquired at the deadline, nor does it cancel out Ward's progress. LB Cedric Gray missed Week 1 due to a concussion, and has still yet to return to the leading role he held last season. The Titans aren't 1-7 because of injuries, but setbacks like these have arguably led to the team ending up on the wrong side of the five one-score games they've lost. Titans' Overloaded Injury Report May Put an Upset Over Jaguars on Ice in Week 10 Skip to main content SI.COM Carnell Tate missing the Tennessee Titans' Week 8 matchup wasn't enough to derail the offense from their best performance of the season. Even in a loss, Tennessee posted 36 points and ground up some real momentum for the first time in weeks heading into the bye. That in itself isn't the issue, but it's hard to really land a hit when you're missing a hand. The Titans, in addition to Tate, will be without LBs Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton, G Peter Skoronski, and P Tommy Townsend. The latter two were sent to the injured reserve list today. Titans are losing major players at the worst possible time This is a team coming apart at the seams at the worst time. One-instance absences - like Tate's in Week 8 - are easier to handle. But the Titans are a 1-7 squad down five starters against the best team in their division. However, it does mean that a Tennessee team down on their luck have caught another bad break. Tennessee can't catch a break this season You'll recall an 0-2 Titans team in a winnable situation on the road watching rookie RG Fernando Carmona Jr. exit vs. the New York Giants. Tennessee lost that game 12-7, and are just now trying to get Carmona back into the swing of things in practice. From that point of view, Week 10's injury report isn't all that surprising. Although, as the season winds down and certain decisions have to be made about this roster prior to an especially important draft, the added pressure from being down impactful talent works against the Titans' rebuilding process. We'll see how the undermanned team fares tomorrow, but for those hoping for a turnaround-sparking upset, you may want to splash cold water on that optimism ahead of time. home.headline: Horrific injuries revealed in Cowboys fan death as family says 49ers supporter blamed by victim
home.blurb: The 36-year-old Dallas Cowboys fan who died after an alleged altercation at AT&T Stadium claimed a 49ers fan pushed him down a flight of stairs, causing a “bulge of blood” in his stomach, according to his heartbroken family. Mario Narro traveled from Albuquerque, New Mexico, to Arlington, Texas, last weekend to watch his beloved Cowboys face the San Francisco 49ers in one of the NFL’s most storied rivalries on Sunday, Nov. 15, his niece Claudia DeLara told the California Post. Narro told a friend he attended the game with that he had gotten into a scuffle and was pushed down a flight of stairs by a Niners fan, DeLara said. “He got pushed,” DeLara exclaimed. “He fell. And immediately he had bruising and swelling in his abdomen.” Narro continued to watch the game after the fall, DeLara said, but after the final whistle on the Niners’ 46-40 victory over the Cowboys, “his friends knew that he was off.” “He wasn’t feeling like his normal self and acting like his normal self and so they made him show them his abdomen just to check to see,” DeLara told The Post. “And they said they could visibly see the bruising and, like, a bulge of blood in his abdomen,” she added. Narro’s friends rushed him to stadium medics, who transported him to a nearby hospital. He continued to insist a Niners fan had pushed him, repeating the account to doctors, DeLara said. Narro then underwent several emergency surgeries, but died from his injuries Wednesday morning. The family is still in the dark as to a specific cause of death, DeLara said. The Tarrant County Medical Examiner is conducting further testing to determine the official cause and manner of Narro’s death. “Nobody really knows what happened,” DeLara added. “We did file a police report because the only thing that we have is [Narro] said that a 49ers fan pushed him. He said that to his friend and the medical team. We don’t know what happened otherwise.” The Arlington Police Department was notified of Narro’s death on Wednesday and is currently “treating this case as a death investigation,” according to a department spokesperson. “The investigation is ongoing,” the APD added. Narro, a lifelong Cowboys fan who loved to travel and crack jokes, had visited AT&T Stadium at least two or three times before Sunday, DeLara said. “He just loved the team,” she said. Narro’s niece, Catalina Jenkins, added that she believes her uncle would still be alive “if it weren’t for this football game.” “I just want it to be clear he was an angel of a man, never hurt anyone, never had anything bad to say about anyone,” Jenkins said. “He was so loved. And I’m so sad he fell victim to such mindless violence.” California Post News: Facebook , Instagram , TikTok , X , YouTube , WhatsApp , LinkedIn California Post Sports Facebook , Instagram , TikTok , YouTube , X California Post App: Download here! home.headline: Cowboys preseason fan favorite returns to Dallas after 2027 UFL draft
home.blurb: Potential was why he was signed by the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent out of the University of Kentucky, so we'll see if the Renegades coaching staff can get the best out out of him. The Renegades are led by hed coach Kevin Sumlin. It will be exciting to see how Pete and Scott perform in the UFL, and it's great that they will be in Dallas so the Cowboys can keep an eye on their progress. Everyone knows Dallas loves to find talent in the spring leagues (Brandon Aubrey, KaVontae Turpin, James Houston), so who knows if a return to the Cowboys could be in the cards if the players put on a show during the 2027 UFL campaign. Cowboys QB Dak Prescott Calls Out DeMarvion Overshown After Foolish Penalty Leading up to the 2026-27 NFL season, there were few players on the Dallas Cowboys roster who were as beloved as Shiyazh Pete. The undrafted free agent offensive lineman was not just a fan favorite in Dallas, but around the league. Pete went viral for an epic post-game speech during the preseason , after his historic appearance. Not only did Pete become the first member of the Navajo Nation to sign with an NFL team, but he also became the first Navajo player to take the field for a game when the Cowboys faced the Arizona Cardinals in the preseason . After that game, he received a standing ovation from thousands of Navajo Nation fans in attendance. The 6-foot-9 Pete was a roster casualty of the Cowboys before the final cuts ahead of the regular season, but now he is returning to Dallas to resume his pro football career. This week, the 2027 NFL Draft was held, and Pete was selected by the Dallas Renegades in Round 8 (No. 59 overall). Shiyazh Pete Gets Great Opportunity To Revive Career The UFL is a perfect opportunity for Pete to get another crack at a professional football career, with his rare combination of size and raw talent setting him up for success if he can continue to develop. Pete wasn't the only former Cowboy to get an opportunity in the UFL this season, with former sixth-round pick Eric Scott Jr. also joining the Dallas Renegades roster. The cornerback, who also spent time with the Kansas City Chiefs and Detroit Lions, was selected in Round 4 (No. 28 overall). However, he's still a better option under center than undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who took first-team reps in practice Wednesday for the Buccaneers. Daniels, who has already started three games this season due to injury issues for Mayfield, has also thrown for more interceptions (five) than touchdowns (three). In fact, Todd Bowles’ squad ranks league worst in several passing categories: attempts (240), yards (1,277) and touchdowns (six). Meanwhile, on defense, Winfield is one of the Buccaneers’ very best players. A two-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro, the longtime Tampa Bay defender has been especially stout against the run in 2026. The 2020 second-round pick has earned an 85.5 Pro Football Focus grade for his efforts against the run, the 13th-best run-defense mark among 100 qualified safeties. Additionally, he hasn't been too shabby against the pass, and has allowed just five receptions all season. And for his efforts in coverage, he's earned a 67.7 grade from PFF, the 24th-best pass-coverage mark among all qualified safeties. Consequently, the Buccaneers, which stand at just 3-6, would hardly be in an optimal situation playing without both Winfield and Mayfield on Sunday. Hutchinson has already been ruled out for the rest of the season, while Campbell is highly unlikely to suit up again in 2026. Detroit, however, is getting back its All-Pro safety for its tilt with Tampa Bay: Kerby Joseph. Joseph – who was activated off the physically unable to perform list Wednesday – hasn't played a single snap since Week 6 of the 2025 season due to a lingering knee issue. Per Lions head man Dan Campbell, Joseph will be on a “pitch count” Sunday, but is still expected to log more snaps than fellow safety Brian Branch did when he returned from his Achilles’ tear earlier this season. Branch played 45 total defensive snaps in his season debut in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers. Prior to Joseph's chronic knee ailment , he was a ball-hawk safety. In 55 career games, he's secured 20 interceptions, including a league-high nine during his All-Pro campaign in 2024. If he can come even remotely close to replicating that level of production, he'll provide a big boost to the back-end of the Lions’ defense. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 76 percent chance to capture the Week 11 victory. picks.blurb: Detroit Lions vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Week Eleven Game Preview and Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch The Ariel Helwani Show The Boys in the Back The Craic with Petesy Carroll The Uncrowned Wrestling Show Inside Boxing The Uncrowned Beat Champions League Premier League Liga MX Apertura Liga MX Clausura The Cooligans Racing Formula 1 MLB trade targets Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended Detroit Lions vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Week Eleven Game Preview and Prediction (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Dakota Allen · Roundtable Sports Sat, November 21, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions (7-2) return home to Ford Field this Sunday, November 22, riding a five-game winning streak and sitting atop the NFC North via divisional tiebreakers. Fresh off a dominant 35-10 international victory over the New England Patriots in Munich, Detroit hosts a Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) squad coming off their bye week. With a massive Thanksgiving showdown against the Chicago Bears looming on Thursday, the Lions must avoid looking ahead against a deceptive Tampa Bay roster. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:00 p.m. EST. Lions' Offensive Juggernaut vs. Bucs' Top-Tier Defense On paper, this matchup is a classic clash of strengths. Detroit enters Week eleven boasting the NFL's top-ranked total offense , averaging 407.6 yards and 28.6 points per game (6th in the league). Running back Jahmyr Gibbs has been playing at an Offensive Player of the Year level, fresh off a 252-scrimmage-yard, two-touchdown explosion in Germany. However, Gibbs and the Lions' ground game face their stiffest test of the season against a Tampa Bay defense that ranks first in the NFL in rushing yards allowed (79.1 per game) and fourth in total yards allowed (292.9 per game). Anchored by Vita Vea and Antoine Winfield Jr., the Buccaneers also lead the league in takeaways with 16 interceptions. For Detroit to keep rolling, Jared Goff and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, who rank third in the league in passing offense at 272.8 yards per game, will need to take advantage of a secondary that can be vulnerable when forced into long-yardage situations. Protecting the football will be paramount for Goff against an opportunistic Tampa Bay defense. Weathering Defensive Injuries Against a One-Dimensional Attack The biggest storyline surrounding Detroit this week is how the defense will respond after suffering devastating injuries to star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson and linebacker Jack Campbell. Prior to those losses, Detroit's front seven had amassed 32 sacks (3rd in the NFL) and held opponents to just 12.8 points per game since their bye week. Getting safety Kerby Joseph back in the lineup alongside Brian Branch will provide a massive boost to the secondary as the defensive line adjusts to life without Hutchinson. Fortunately for Detroit, Tampa Bay's offense has struggled to find balance under new coordinator Zac Robinson. While the Buccaneers own the league's No. 1 rushing attack at 163.9 yards per game, leaning heavily on Bucky Irving and controlling the clock for over 32 minutes per contest, their passing game ranks dead last at 158.1 yards per game. Without franchise legends Mike Evans and Lavonte David, who departed in the offseason, Baker Mayfield has lacked consistent aerial firepower, especially with wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. and Irving dealing with practice absences this week. If Detroit's interior defensive line, led by Alim McNeill, can clog running lanes and force Mayfield into obvious passing downs, the Lions' depleted pass rush will have plenty of opportunities to make plays. Game Prediction Tampa Bay's elite run defense and ball-hawking secondary should prevent Detroit from turning this into an early blowout, and the Buccaneers' commitment to the ground game will shorten the contest. Ultimately, however, Tampa Bay simply lacks the passing efficiency to trade blows with Detroit on the fast track at Ford Field. Expect Dan Campbell's squad to lean on Goff, St. Brown, and Gibbs' versatility in the passing game to overcome Tampa Bay's front seven, pulling away late to secure their sixth consecutive victory. Final Score Prediction: Detroit Lions 27, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 17

On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.” The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

home.blurb: After missing Wednesday's practice, quarterback Baker Mayfield (foot/right thumb) returned to the practice field Thursday as a limited participant. While his return to practice is certainly encouraging, the Buccaneers are expected to make a determination on his availability Friday. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels remains the next man up should Mayfield be unable to play. Unfortunately for Tampa Bay, safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) missed his second consecutive practice, while outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) remained limited. Wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. and running back Bucky Irving were added to Thursday's injury report as non-participants, while defensive lineman A'Shawn Robinson was limited. All three received rest designations. For Detroit, there were no changes to its injury report from Wednesday. Center Cade Mays (ankle) remained sidelined, while six players, including cornerbacks D.J. Reed (hip) and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder), remained limited. picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for Cardinals at Chiefs, Starting With Michael Wilson Topping 100 Yards
3 Bold Predictions for Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11
picks.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals are 3-7 and headed to Arrowhead Stadium to face a 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs team that just beat Atlanta 35-13. They’ll do it with a 40-year-old quarterback, after Mike LaFleur said rookie Carson Beck’s back spasms have the team preparing Josh Johnson to start . Nobody expects much from Arizona in this one. Here are three bold predictions for Sunday’s noon CT kickoff. 1. Michael Wilson tops 100 receiving yards Kansas City’s defensive plan starts with Trey McBride, who has 78 catches and draws most of the short throws in this offense . That leaves Wilson as the receiver most likely to see single coverage. He has 51 catches for 546 yards, according to ESPN , second on the team behind McBride. We ran his numbers, and they show a receiver who gets volume without many big plays. Wilson has caught 51 of his 89 targets, about 57%, and he’s averaging 60.7 yards per game with a long of 27. A 100-yard day needs one or two downfield completions, and a veteran quarterback who’s been around 15 NFL rosters knows where his second option is. 2. Josh Johnson throws two touchdown passes Johnson is 2-9 in 11 career starts , and Sunday would be his first start since last season with Washington. Arizona has only 13 passing touchdowns in 10 games, and it has scored touchdowns on 42.9% of its red-zone trips. That’s why two touchdown passes is a bold call. Johnson played three games for LaFleur’s Jets in 2021, so he knows the system, and he has McBride as an easy red-zone target. If the Cardinals keep the game close into the second half, Johnson finds him twice. 3. Arizona holds Kansas City under 100 rushing yards This one goes against everything from last week. The Rams ran 46 times for 202 yards against Arizona, and the Cardinals lost two defenders to injured reserve before this trip. Arizona allows 129.9 rushing yards per game, 28th in the league. Kenneth Walker III changes the math, though. He has 872 of Kansas City’s 1,224 rushing yards, about 71%, and he missed practice again Thursday with a groin injury, according to Heavy . If Walker sits for a second straight week, the Chiefs will lean on Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce. Arizona keeps the run game in check and makes Kansas City win it through the air. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said the team isn't closing the door on Beck playing Sunday, though they're preparing for their fourth starting quarterback in as many weeks with Josh Johnson now expected to be under center. away.headline: Rams Week 10 injury report vs. Cardinals: Puka Nacua is on IR, so who will step up for LA?
away.blurb: Tyler Higbee stands out as the main weapon to build around in Nacua's absence, particularly on intermediate routes and crucial possession downs. His experience with Stafford makes him a logical candidate for additional attention, although that projection should not be mistaken for an announced target distribution. Higbee's own health briefly complicated that outlook. An illness kept him out Thursday before he returned for limited work Friday. He received no game designation, leaving him available for an offense that needs dependable receiving options. The tight end group's other injuries make his role especially important. Terrance Ferguson is out with ankle and hamstring injuries, while Davis Allen is questionable with an oblique issue. Colby Parkinson offers another available option after progressing to full participation Friday despite injured ribs. Tutu Atwell can provide a different dimension outside. His ability to threaten downfield offers a way to discourage Arizona from crowding shorter routes. Stafford connected with him for a 40-yard gain against the Chargers in Week 8, demonstrating the explosive element available beyond the depleted starting group. CJ Daniels Jr., Xavier Smith and newly promoted Brennan Presley round out the available receiver group. The Rams placed Nacua on IR Thursday to create the roster opening for Presley; Nacua must miss at least four games, making this adjustment more than a one-week assignment. Beyond Nacua's absence, Steve Avila is ruled out after missing every practice with a hamstring injury. Losing an offensive lineman adds another complication as the Rams reshape their passing attack, especially if Stafford needs extra time for unfamiliar combinations to develop. Allen's questionable designation follows limited practices Wednesday and Friday around a missed Thursday session. Long snapper Joe Cardona is also questionable after remaining limited throughout the week with an ankle injury. Defensively, Myles Garrett carries a questionable designation for a knee issue and rest. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out Friday. His availability matters after a three-sack performance against Washington helped Los Angeles secure its third consecutive victory. Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl are questionable, too. Both returned for limited work Friday after two missed sessions, managing back and toe injuries, respectively. Braden Fiske missed Friday with an ankle injury but received no game designation. Byron Young and Aaron Donald also sat out for rest without designations, distinguishing their absences from confirmed injury-related setbacks. home.headline: Kenneth Walker injury update, latest NFL rumors on Chiefs RB recovery timeline
home.blurb: After sitting out Sunday's win over the Atlanta Falcons while recovering from a groin injury, Kansas City Chiefs star running back Kenneth Walker III will miss a little more time. Walker was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals, marking the second-straight game the running back will miss. After sitting out on Sunday, Walker still ranks fourth in the NFL with 872 rushing yards. After signing with Kansas City in free agency over the offseason, he's provided a different dimension to an offense that has long relied on Mahomes' heroics. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters Wednesday that the team didn't want to do "something stupid" in regards to Walker's groin injury, but noted the running back was "feeling better." During an appearance on Monday's episode of The Pat McAfee Show , ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Chiefs' "idea was to shut [Walker] down for a week" because they "believe that it's a short-term injury." Even without Walker, the Chiefs cruised to a 35-13 victory over the Falcons. Emmitt Johnson racked up a career-high 101 yards on 22 carries while adding six receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns. Star quarterback Patrick Mahomes was in top form, throwing for 348 yards, five touchdowns and no interceptions. Still, Schefter made it clear that the Chiefs will be cautious with Walker's recovery, especially after Johnson's impressive performance. Walker has a history of soft-tissue injuries, and Kansas City will want him healthy for the playoffs. "There's really not a rush to bring him back when Emmett Johnson is playing the way he is," Schefter said. "So, would it surprise me if it went beyond this week? No. They'll have to see how he's feeling. They did not consider it to be a long-term type of issue when he hurt his groin in practice on Thursday." In Week 11, the Chiefs will be facing a Cardinals team that ranks 28th in the NFL with 129.9 rushing yards allowed per game, so they can afford to let Walker rest for another week while Johnson takes the reins.

home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs' final injury report for Week 11 vs. Arizona Cardinals confirms the team will be shorthanded on offense
home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their final injury report ahead of Week 11's game against the Arizona Cardinals. After practice on Friday, Chiefs HC Andy Reid confirmed a third straight missed practice for three players on the offensive side of the ball. “The guys who didn't practice today were Jaylon Moore, Trey Smith, and Ken Walker,” Reid said. “All of which are improving.” Reid said all three players would likely be ruled out for the game. The decision on Walker was expected after NFL Insiders reported earlier this week that Kansas City could sit him for a second game. Emmett Johnson is expected to get his second career start on Sunday. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related It looks like it'll be another week for Chiefs DT Omarr Norman-Lott, who continues to work his way back from his 2025 knee injury. He was activated to the 53-man roster earlier this week . He's been limited in every practice session since the team opened his 21-day practice window. DT Peter Woods was downgraded to limited participation during Friday's practice session. He has missed the past two games with his neck injury. Kansas City Chiefs' final injury report for Week 11 vs. Arizona Cardinals confirms the team will be shorthanded on offense Skip to content College Football Close Menu All College Football The Kansas City Chiefs released their final Week 11 injury report vs. the Arizona Cardinals. It looks like they'll be shorthanded again on offense. Smith and Moore's absences will leave the Chiefs with replacements across the entire right side of the offensive line. Asked about the O-line situation this week, specifically about any changes at right guard, Coach Reid described it as kind of like a preseason game. “Well, we've got a variety there, but they're all going to have a shot to get in there and go,” Reid said. “So, we'll see how it all goes, but I think everybody has a lot of trust in Mike (Caliendo) if he's the one in there playing.” Here’s a quick breakdown of each team’s Week 11 injury report, complete with game status designations. It hasn’t been the season the Eagles have hoped for, as injuries and trades have decimated their roster. They’ve lost seven games in a row since starting the season 2-0, but are coming out of their bye week. On the other hand, the Steelers won four games in a row prior to last week’s 38-18 loss at Cincinnati. They still sit at 6-3 on the season, though, and are in the playoff picture in their conference – that’s more than the Eagles can say. The Eagles have won the last two meetings, and the Steelers haven’t won in Philadelphia since 1965 (a stretch of 11 matchups), but that could change this week.
