picks.headline: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football MLB trade targets Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. picks.blurb: Steelers vs Eagles betting guide: Odds, props and picks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football MLB trade targets Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended Steelers vs Eagles betting guide: Odds, props and picks Dan Roche · NBC Sports Philadelphia Sat, November 21, 2026 at 7:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Steelers vs Eagles betting guide: Odds, props and picks originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia All odds courtesy FanDuel Sports Book Steelers (6-3) vs Eagles (2-7), Sunday 1:00pm Point spread/ML: Steelers -4.5/-225 Eagles +4.5/+188 Total: 37.5 points Analysis: The Steelers have had a strong season, coming in at 6-3. They had won four straight before being embarrassed on national television by the Bengals, 38-18. The Eagles are no strangers to embarrassment this season, but for the first time in several weeks, the injury report isn't looking like a CVS receipt. WR DeVonta Smith practiced in full Thursday, as did RB Saquon Barkley, and edge rushers Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt. HC Mike McCarthy is in his first season coaching Pittsburgh, but has plenty of experience coaching against the Eagles from his days in Green Bay and Dallas. He is 3-5 lifetime in games at the Linc. Nick Sirianni is 5-0 after a bye week, but I'm not sure any amount of time will give his team enough of an advantage. Picks: Steelers -4.5 Passing Props (O/U) Aaron Rodgers: 211.5 passing yards, 1.5 TD (+140/-188) Joe Milton: 187.5 passing yards, 0.5 TD (-205/+152) Analysis: Milton did his best with the hand he was dealt two weeks ago against the Giants (18/34/169), considering he spent much of the afternoon running for his life. He'll get help with Smith – and very possibly Tay Wicks – returning to the lineup. He should also get a boost from a Steelers pass D ranked 30 th in the league. Rodgers has had an up-and-down season; he had a four-week run where he looked bulletproof, and followed it up with two games with subpar numbers: a blowout win over Cleveland, where they didn't need much from him, and their blowout loss to the Bengals, where they didn't get much. Picks: Milton OVER yards, Rodgers OVER yards Rushing Props (O/U) Jaylen Warren – 65.5 yards Saquon Barkley – 60.5 yards Rico Dowdle – 37.5 yards Milton – 34.5 yards Analysis: I feel a lot of the game script could be determined by which Jaylen Warren shows up. He has had five games with 93+ yards this season, and four with 50 or fewer, the most recent last week vs Cincy (7/15). Dowdle had three straight games of 40+ yards before last week's 5/26. I like Milton to make more plays with his legs, as he did vs NYG (9/64). It may be a better strategy than running Barkley between the tackles. Barkley may finally be healthy, but he can't block for himself. Picks: Barkley UNDER yards, Milton OVER yards Receiving Props (O/U) DeVonta Smith – 48.5 yards, 4.5 receptions DK Metcalf – 42.5 yards, 3.5 receptions Dallas Goedert – 30.5 yards, 3.5 receptions Germie Bernard – 29.5 yards, 3.5 receptions Warren – 22.5 yards, 2.5 receptions Pat Freiermuth – 20.5 yards, 2.5 receptions Darnell Washington 20.5 yards, 2.5 receptions Barkley – 10.5 yards, 1.5 receptions Dowdle – 9.5 yards, 1.5 receptions Analysis: One would think Smith will want to put on a show after missing 5 of the last 6 games, and a change in QB from Tanner McKee to Milton shouldn't put a wrinkle in that. Goedert has caught 4+ passes in L5. I can't explain what happened to DK Metcalf. 35 catches in nine games is far less than I expected, and I think Steelers fans would agree. Five catches on 28 targets over the last 3 weeks is shocking. Meanwhile, Bernard had a four-game run of 25 catches before being shutout last week. Warren has 3 catches in 6/9 this season, and 26+ yards in 8/9, he's Rodgers' main checkdown option. Picks: Smith OVER yards, OVER receptions; Warren OVER receptions, OVER yards Anytime Touchdown Washington +300 Freiermuth +330 Analysis: Either Steelers TE has scored in six straight. Play them both, just not in a parlay. Picks: Barkley, Milton, Washington, Freiermuth

picks.headline: Eagles vs. Steelers: 5 bold predictions for the Week 11 matchup
picks.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
picks.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles are running out of time to find something resembling an offensive identity. There's hope that the defense catches fire before it's too late. Seven consecutive losses have turned what once looked like a promising season into a weekly search for answers. What's fortunate (or unfortunate depending on your paradigm) is that they're still right in the thick of things in the NFC East. They're four games behind the division-leading New York Giants with seven games remaining. As bad as all four teams have played at times, any team can go on a run or a losing streak and change the complexion of this race for superiority. The upcoming matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers offers another opportunity to see whether anything has changed for the better. The bye week gave Joe Milton extra time to get comfortable with his surroundings and the coaching staff time to address some glaring problems. A turnaround remains difficult to envision, but there are reasons to expect a more competitive performance than Philadelphia has delivered recently. Here are a handful of predictions for the coming contest that reflect both that possibility and the larger issues that continue to hold the Eagles back. DeVonta Smith returns and notches 100 yards receiving while Makai Lemon chips in with 50 DeVonta Smith was very blunt this week . He didn't work so hard during the offseason to 'shut it down' with so many games remaining. "I didn’t get up at 4:30 in the morning all summer just to not play." After limited participation at practice on Wednesday , he got his legs under him a day later and was a full participant on Thursday . He says he's 100 percent healthy. Something tells us an offensively starved Eagles attack will get him the ball early and often against the Steelers . He'll lead the Eagles in targets, receptions, and yards gained. Figure 100 of the latter, but that doesn't mean Makai Lemon will be forgotten. He and Milton have worked together for a while, and that level of comfort should guarantee the former looks for his young rookie to pay dividends. Lemon already showed what his role can look like with Milton. He led the Eagles with six catches for 61 yards on nine targets against the Giants . If Smith returns, Philadelphia can use him outside while keeping Lemon involved on quick throws from the slot. That gives both receivers a path to the yardage totals without asking Milton to spend the afternoon waiting on deep routes. Joe Milton plays turnover-free football There is still plenty to like about Joe Milton's physical ability, but his first start was an especially difficult introduction to life in the NFL . He was thrown into the lineup less than a month after joining the team, behind an offensive line that offered little protection. Even a quarterback with Joe Burrow's experience and ability would have faced a difficult assignment under those circumstances. Milton now has a start behind him and a bye week to prepare for Pittsburgh. He said he would spend much of that time in Philadelphia to build familiarity with the offense and his teammates. A spectacular performance might be too much to expect, but protecting the football and avoiding costly mistakes would represent meaningful progress. Milton went without an interception against New York, but he lost a fumble on a strip-sack by Arvell Reese. Against Pittsburgh, protecting the ball starts with having an answer when the first read is covered and the rush closes in. A checkdown or a throwaway can keep a drive alive without giving the Steelers a short field. Aaron Rodgers throws two interceptions Aaron Rodgers has thrown at least one interception in five of Pittsburgh's nine games this season, and he's been bailed out a few times in games where he hasn't. That's an opportunity Vic Fangio and the Eagles defense should be prepared to exploit, particularly if the pass rush can make the veteran quarterback uncomfortable. Rodgers is experienced enough to recognize pressure and punish defensive mistakes, so forcing him into difficult decisions will be important. Still, Philadelphia has shown it can create disruptive moments defensively. The bold prediction here is that Fangio's unit comes away with two interceptions, even if the Eagles fail to turn both takeaways into points. Two interceptions would be a significant jump for a defense that enters Week 11 with three all season. The best chance starts with pressure from four rushers. If Philadelphia can hurry Rodgers and keep seven defenders in coverage, it can leave help over DK Metcalf while keeping a defender available to break on a shorter throw. Eagles score 20 points despite being one-dimensional Philadelphia's offense has struggled to establish a reliable ground game, and there isn't much reason to expect that the problem has disappeared. Sure, everyone is hopeful, but many have also taken the 'We'll believe it when we see it' approach. Here's the good news. The Steelers have allowed 242.2 passing yards per game. If protection holds up, Milton and the passing attack an opportunity to find some rhythm. The prediction is that Philadelphia hangs a number slightly above Pittsburgh's average. Figure approximately 250 yards through the air thanks to Lemon and some returning reinforcements. The Eagles haven't scored 24 points (a season high) since Week 2. They haven't topped 20 for two weeks, but what the heck? These are bold predictions, right? Call it stubborn. Call it insanity, since a quiet day from the running game is also part of this prediction. Philadelphia hasn't offered a consistent, sustainable formula, but a surprisingly successful air raid and fewer three-and-outs could make this game more high-scoring than expected. Philadelphia loses a game that's closer than most would expect We hate to disappoint you. After all of that, you may have had your fingers crossed for an upset, but the facts are the facts. Right now, Pittsburgh is the better team. The Eagles have opportunities to finally put some points on the board, but Philadelphia has lost seven straight for a reason. As always, the home crowd will be supportive enough to try to provide a spark for a team that desperately needs one. Still, a better offensive showing doesn't automatically solve the team's larger problems. The defense can keep the Eagles within striking distance for much of the afternoon, but eventually the offense must make enough plays to win. Sadly, none of us have seen them do that enough to believe they'll get it done in this scenario. Milton provides a few encouraging moments, but Pittsburgh does enough to offer Philadelphia an eighth consecutive loss. A more watchable performance and a winning result are two very different things, and Philadelphia still has a long way to go before those outcomes become interchangeable. Prediction: Steelers 27, Eagles 20 This article originally appeared on Eagles Wire: Eagles vs. Steelers: 5 bold predictions for the Week 11 matchup

Financial Field on Sunday for a game against their instate rival, the Philadelphia Eagles (2-7). Although on the road, this game comes at a critical point in the Steelers’ season. With games the next three weeks against the Broncos, the Texans, and the Jaguars - all teams contending for a playoff spot in the AFC - this one is a near must-win against the Birds. Second in the AFC North and sixth in the AFC overall, Aaron Rodgers and co. are a half-game ahead of the Browns and 1.5 games ahead of the Patriots in the postseason chase. The Eagles have struggled for most of the season. Jalen Hurts led Philly to wins in their first two games, but the Eagles have since lost every game as well as their quarterback (blood clots). This season, the Steelers have leaned on Rodgers, a productive running game and a defense that ranks among the league leaders in sacks and turnover differential. The veteran signal-caller has thrown for 2,014 yards with 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, while Jaylen Warren has rushed for 719 yards. Philadelphia’s season has unraveled in large part because of injuries, most notably the aforementioned loss of Hurts to injured reserve with blood clots. That leaves Joe Milton III directing an Eagles offense averaging just 16.4 points and an NFL-low 260.2 yards per game. Pittsburgh’s four-game winning streak came to an abrupt end last Sunday in a 38-18 road loss to Cincinnati. The Bengals completely suffocated the Steelers with Pittsburgh managing only 23 total yards through the first three quarters before producing some offense and points after the game was out of reach. DK Metcalf was held without a catch through three quarters before finishing with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown, while the defense spent far too much time on the field. Philadelphia, meanwhile, comes into Sunday’s game rested after its bye but desperately searching for an answer to a disastrous stretch. The Eagles’ most recent game was a 19-11 home loss to the Giants on Nov. 8. Milton made his first Eagles start and completed 18 of 34 passes for just 169 yards. It has been a weekly headline for Philadelphia: “Eagles’ are Offensive on Offense”. The bye, though, may help an injury-ravaged roster: receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could return after missing the Giants game. Smith’s availability is especially significant because the Eagles badly need another proven weapon alongside Saquon Barkley to make life easier for Milton against a Pittsburgh defense featuring T.J. Watt and one of the NFL’s better pass rushes. Beyond Pittsburgh’s attempt to rebound and Philadelphia’s effort to stop its seven-game skid, the matchup carries a fascinating piece of Pennsylvania rivalry history. The Eagles lead the all-time series 50-29-3, and Pittsburgh has endured an extraordinary drought in Philadelphia. The Steelers have not won in Philly since 1965. They have lost their last 11 games against the Eagles in the City of Brotherly Love. Philadelphia has also dominated the two most recent meetings, winning 27-13 in Philadelphia on Dec. 15, 2024, after a 35-13 home victory in 2022; Pittsburgh’s last win in the series was a 38-29 victory at Heinz Field in 2020. Updated Nov 18, 2026 at 11:38am The Philadelphia Eagles aren't the only team dealing with injuries on the offense for Week 11. On the other side, the Pittsburgh Steelers just got a notable injury update for their starting guard, Mason McCormick. For a moment, it seemed the Steelers could be looking at a long-term setback for McCormick–potentially season-ending–but a report from ESPN states that's likely not the case. Pittsburgh Steelers guard Mason McCormick suffered a dislocated ankle but does not have a fracture, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, leaving him with a chance of returning during the playoffs. McCormick was carted off the field in an air cast after being injured in the second quarter of Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. But sources told Rapoport that McCormick does not need surgery and that the ankle was popped back into place on the field. via ESPN. While McCormick received good news on the injury front, it's not going to make a difference for Sunday's action between the Eagles and Steelers. Pittsburgh will miss the starting guard. The Eagles catch a slight break there. The 2026 NFL season has been a roller coaster for the Eagles' defense. At times, they flashed elite play, mirroring the past two seasons. However, a lack of pressure and struggles in the secondary have shown up at times as well. It's unclear which version the Steelers' offense will see this week in Philadelphia, but the Eagles are going to have to work through a major change. It's the first week without Jordan Davis up front. The veteran defensive tackle was traded ahead of the deadline. Davis is a new member of the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Eagles still have Jalen Carter and Moro Ojomo headlining the unit, and recently added Leki Fotu to the practice squad for a potential call-up on Sunday. away.headline: Steelers vs. Eagles Injury Report
away.blurb: Wide receiver DeVonta Smith is good to go for Sunday's game against the Steelers, but Dontayvion Wicks remains out. The Eagles are healthier coming out of the bye week and will welcome the return of wide receiver DeVonta Smith to the lineup on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. However, the Eagles will be without Smith's positionmate Dontayvion Wicks for the fourth game in a row. Wicks was limited in practice all week with an ankle injury. The team added a foot injury for Wicks on Friday's report. Linebacker Smael Mondon is doubtful for Sunday's game after missing the past two practices with an ankle injury. Running back Will Shipley did not practice on Friday due to an illness. He is questionable as he remains on Injured Reserve with a foot injury. He would need to be activated off Injured Reserve to the 53-man roster by 4 PM on Saturday to be eligible to play against the Steelers. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell is set to return to the lineup and start alongside Jeremiah Trotter Jr. with Baun out and Mondon doubtful. Campbell missed the past two games with hamstring and quad injuries. Defensive back Michael Carter missed three of the last four games with an abdomen injury. Wide receiver Britain Covey was out for the last two games with a knee injury. Cornerback Jonathan Jones is healthy after missing the past two games with a hamstring injury. The Steelers listed six players as questionable, including outside linebacker Nick Herbig, who suffered injuries to his hip and ribs last Sunday night in Cincinnati. Herbig did not practice all week. Three of the players who are questionable – guard Gennings Dunker, wide receiver Michael Pittman, and wide receiver Roman Wilson – are on Injured Reserve and, like Shipley for the Eagles, would need to be activated in order to play against Philadelphia. Wide receiver DeVonta Smith was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday after practicing in a limited capacity Wednesday. Smith told reporters after Wednesday's practice that he was back to 100 percent after missing five of the last six games with a hamstring injury. Linebacker Smael Mondon joined fellow linebacker Zack Baun on the sideline Thursday. Mondon was a full participant with an ankle injury on Wednesday, but did not participate in practice Thursday. Mondon stepped in during the Week 9 game against the Giants before the bye week after Baun suffered a back injury and Jihaad Campbell was out with hamstring and quad injuries. Baun has yet to practice this week, while Campbell is on track to return. Running back Will Shipley, practicing for the first time since the Week 5 game in London, was limited for the second straight day. The Eagles would need to activate him off of Injured Reserve to be eligible for Sunday's game. RB Will Shipley and WR Dontayvion Wicks spotted! Updated Nov 18, 2026 at 11:38am The Philadelphia Eagles aren't the only team dealing with injuries on the offense for Week 11. On the other side, the Pittsburgh Steelers just got a notable injury update for their starting guard, Mason McCormick. For a moment, it seemed the Steelers could be looking at a long-term setback for McCormick–potentially season-ending–but a report from ESPN states that's likely not the case. Pittsburgh Steelers guard Mason McCormick suffered a dislocated ankle but does not have a fracture, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, leaving him with a chance of returning during the playoffs. McCormick was carted off the field in an air cast after being injured in the second quarter of Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. But sources told Rapoport that McCormick does not need surgery and that the ankle was popped back into place on the field. via ESPN. While McCormick received good news on the injury front, it's not going to make a difference for Sunday's action between the Eagles and Steelers. Pittsburgh will miss the starting guard. The Eagles catch a slight break there. The 2026 NFL season has been a roller coaster for the Eagles' defense. At times, they flashed elite play, mirroring the past two seasons. However, a lack of pressure and struggles in the secondary have shown up at times as well. It's unclear which version the Steelers' offense will see this week in Philadelphia, but the Eagles are going to have to work through a major change. It's the first week without Jordan Davis up front. The veteran defensive tackle was traded ahead of the deadline. Davis is a new member of the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Eagles still have Jalen Carter and Moro Ojomo headlining the unit, and recently added Leki Fotu to the practice squad for a potential call-up on Sunday. With the Eagles season in 2026 looking like a lost year, though, the wideout faced a question Wednesday about whether he should have dressed in Week 5. Smith clearly didn't care for that suggestion. The wideout, though, told reporters Wednesday he was 100% for the game. At that point, Smith then launched into his tirade about wanting to still play despite the team's 2-7 record. Whether Smith interpreted the line of questioning as implying the team should give up on the season or if the wideout just simply addressed the topic on his own is unclear. away.headline: NFL fans react to Ravens’ rumored plan for Lamar Jackson’s return after thumb injury
away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens believe Lamar Jackson has a chance to return from his broken right thumb for their Week 16 game against the Cleveland Browns on Dec. 27 if his rehab goes smoothly, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported this week. Lamar Jackson’s Road From Buffalo Toward a Possible Browns Return In a statement the team released that day, head coach Jesse Minter called recovery timelines “challenging to predict” and said, “He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Minter added, “We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season.” Graziano’s report hinges on Jackson’s progress in the same way, leaving the Browns game at M&T Bank Stadium a possibility rather than a set date for his return. For another fan, the calendar is the problem, since a return against the Browns would leave Jackson only two more regular-season games after that one. A Dec. 27 return would be near the optimistic end of Jackson’s reported recovery timetable, though the Ravens have emphasized that his progress, rather than a fixed date, will determine when he can play again. The report comes with Baltimore at 4-6, days after a 23-20 home loss to the Los Angeles Chargers, who had not won a game before Monday night. Despite the prospect of Jackson returning for the final stretch of the regular season, several fans who responded to the report argued that the Ravens should keep him sidelined and focus on having him healthy for 2027. Jackson’s injury came on Baltimore’s first offensive play of the Nov. 1 game at Buffalo, a 36-10 loss, when his throwing hand caught the arm of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau as he threw. On Nov. 13, the Ravens said the thumb was dislocated and broken and that the injury typically carries a recovery of six to 10 weeks. Sources told ESPN’s Adam Schefter that Jackson had undergone surgery the week before. Fans Point to the Baltimore Ravens’ Slide and Jackson’s Long-Term Health “Week 16 is so late. Just shut him down and run it back next year,” the fan wrote. Baltimore’s form has added to the argument. The Ravens sit fourth in the AFC North and have lost five straight games, including the Buffalo game in which Jackson was hurt and both games since. Jacoby Brissett, whom Baltimore acquired in a trade, started in Jackson’s place in the loss to the Chargers. “It’s already over … just take the rest of the season off,” another fan responded. Jackson’s health is another piece of it. A high ankle sprain had already cost him three games before the thumb injury, and he has played just 14 full quarters this season. A fan pointed to that history: “Yea bro let’s have Lamar play meaningless games in a lost season after 2 major injuries.” Others looked straight ahead to next season. “What’s the point to play him at that point, come back ’27 stronger,” one fan wrote. Madubuike left Monday night’s 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers and was ruled out in the third quarter. Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday the Ravens would evaluate how the hamstring responds later in the week. Ioane was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated report with knee and shoulder injuries after leaving the Chargers game in the third quarter. His upgrade is an encouraging sign for an offensive line that helped produce just 16 rushing yards Monday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remained limited with a knee injury. Running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring), tight end Matt Hibner (hand) and outside linebacker Mike Green (biceps) were listed as full participants for a second straight day. Carolina tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble were listed as limited Thursday with knee injuries after both were listed as nonparticipants Wednesday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins is the lone player ruled out, while running back Adam Randall is questionable. That leaves Baltimore in a favorable position compared to its opponent. For the most part, Baltimore should have the majority of its roster available. The biggest concern remains Jackson's absence, which puts even more pressure on Brissett to provide enough offense to keep the Ravens competitive. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey is the biggest name ruled out for Los Angeles. His absence takes away an important piece of the passing game, making life more difficult for an offense that has struggled to find consistency. Five other players are listed as questionable: guard Kayode Awosika, defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe, tight end David Njoku, linebacker Denzel Perryman and offensive tackle Trey Pipkins. The good news is that the rest of the players on the report should be available Monday night, barring any last-minute changes. That gives Los Angeles a chance to avoid an even longer list of absences, but the players already ruled out and those carrying questionable designations could still make an impact. home.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike misses second practice before Panthers game
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike missed practice for a second straight day Thursday with a hamstring injury, while rookie right guard Vega Ioane was upgraded to full participation ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers . Madubuike left Monday night’s 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers and was ruled out in the third quarter. Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday the Ravens would evaluate how the hamstring responds later in the week. Ioane was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated report with knee and shoulder injuries after leaving the Chargers game in the third quarter. His upgrade is an encouraging sign for an offensive line that helped produce just 16 rushing yards Monday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remained limited with a knee injury. Running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring), tight end Matt Hibner (hand) and outside linebacker Mike Green (biceps) were listed as full participants for a second straight day. Carolina tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble were listed as limited Thursday with knee injuries after both were listed as nonparticipants Wednesday. Running back Chuba Hubbard returned to full participation after a rest day, and outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (ankle) was upgraded from limited to full. Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and safety Isaiah Simmons (knee) remained out of practice. Young (foot) and cornerbacks Will Lee III (hamstring) and Mike Jackson (groin) were listed as full participants for the second straight day. Jackson remains in his return-to-practice window and would need to be activated from injured reserve to play Sunday. The teams’ Friday reports will provide the official game designations. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey was added to Thursday’s report as a nonparticipant for personal reasons. Minter sent Humphrey home Thursday and said the cornerback will be inactive Sunday. The decision came a day after Humphrey apologized for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” Vega Ioane upgraded to full participation Madubuike’s status is the main injury question for Baltimore heading into Friday. His availability will help determine how the Ravens rotate their interior linemen against Carolina and how much pressure they can generate up the middle against Bryce Young. Humphrey’s absence also changes the coverage rotation against a Panthers receiving group led by Tetairoa McMillan. After winning their first game of the 2026 season, it is going to be interesting to see how LA approaches the rest of the season , and whether they are competitive or end up with a top draft pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That said, the focus now moves to their home matchup this week against the New York Jets in a game that could have a lot to do with how the draft order pans out. On that note, ESPN put out a Week 11 preview done by NFL Nation as well as fantasy football writer Eric Moody, analytics writer Seth Walder, and sports betting analyst Pamela Maldonado, who picked each game, and when it came to the Chargers and Jets matchup, LA was the unanimous pick. Now, in terms of the picks, Maldonado had the Chargers winning 24-20, Moody had a 23-17 victory for LA, and Walder picked Los Angeles to 23-20. All that to say, it is very clear that this ESPN panel does like the Chargers this week, and despite the fact the season has been rough for LA thus far, sometimes after picking up a win, a team can get into a rhythm and start stacking wins. One thing to note on the Chargers side, is the fact that they did a great job on the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball on Monday night against the Ravens. Starting with the defense, LA held running back Derrick Henry to 10 yards rushing on 10 carries and the Ravens 15 attempts for 16 yards as a team. That is a great performance for LA and because of that, it forced quarterback Jacoby Brissett to put the the game on his shoulders and the Chargers were able to do just enough to get the win through picking him off once and recovering a fumble from wide receiver Zay Flowers. Now on the offensive side, the Chargers ran the ball very well with running back Omarion Hampton tallying 22 carries for 105 yards and one score in addition to quarterback Justin Herbert adding seven carries for 51 yards and a touchdown. As a team, LA ran the ball 34 times for 160 yards while averaging 4.7 yards per carry. All that to say, the formula for the Chargers in Week 10 was dominating on both sides of the line of scrimmage which worked out and enabled them to pick up a win which was huge for their confidence, but also shows that they do not need to lean on Herbert. So, as the Chargers prepare to take on the Jets in Week 11, it will be interesting to see if LA can pick up another win, but also what the formula might be, because if Los Angeles once again dominates up front, that could be something that the Chargers can lean on for the rest of the year.

picks.headline: New York Jets vs. Los Angeles Chargers Odds and Predictions
picks.blurb: Latest Teams On Air Listen + Watch Contests Events More LISTEN LIVE Home The New York Jets will visit the Los Angeles Chargers at 4:05 p.m. ET on Sunday in a game that has more implications for the draft than it does for… Ezra Bernstein Updated Nov 20, 2026 9:55 AM EST Share this story The New York Jets will visit the Los Angeles Chargers at 4:05 p.m. ET on Sunday in a game that has more implications for the draft than it does for the postseason. New York has lost five contests in a row, the last two of which were blowout defeats at the hands of the Kansas City Chiefs and the Buffalo Bills. While the Chargers are technically headed in the other direction after securing their first win of the year, Los Angeles still looks like one of the worst teams in football on a week-to-week basis. Getting a second consecutive win would be a good start in changing that perception. While New York is coming off a couple of blowout losses, those defeats did come against a few of the best teams in football. When head coach Aaron Glenn's squad faced teams like the New England Patriots, Miami Dolphins, and Las Vegas Raiders, the Jets hung tough, losing each game on the outcome of one or two plays. If those performances are any indication, New York should be plenty capable of keeping things close with the Chargers. Quarterback Geno Smith will have to play a turnover-free game, while the defense, led by rookie defensive end David Bailey, plays mistake-free football. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel finally seemed to get things to click in the Chargers' last game against the Baltimore Ravens. Giving running back Omarion Hampton an extended run for the first time in ages helped revive a ground attack that seemed dead in the water only a couple of weeks ago. If McDaniel knows what's good for his job security, he will give Hampton the touches he earned last week. Denver held on for a narrow 10-7 win, but it came at the cost of losing starting running back J.K. Dobbins for the season. Yeah, Broncos-Raiders tends to get chippy. When it comes to divisional rivalries and the matchups that come with them, all bets are off. The Broncos are emerging from their bye and are about as healthy as they could hope to be, while the Raiders are settling into life with rookie Fernando Mendoza under center after trading away Kirk Cousins early last week. Sean Payton has an excellent record coming off the bye — 17-6 (.739) — but Klint Kubiak's Raiders are hungry. It could be a rock-fight on Sunday. Look for Jonah Coleman to have a big day on the ground — notching his first-career 100-yard rushing performance — while Nix passes for 250 yards and two touchdowns. Fernando Mendoza gets acquainted with the Mile High turf, as the Broncos sack the No. 1 overall pick in this year's draft five times. They currently sit at 7-2, are in the hunt for the AFC West title and the top seed in the AFC. Even better is the week off should allow the Broncos to get players back from injury, especially on defense. All of this to say Denver is in a great spot. Now come the hated Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, led by rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. The Broncos want to build on this great start to the season and carry the momentum over from the bye this Sunday against their rivals. Denver is a massive -10-point home favorite against the Raiders (4-6) at FanDuel Sportsbook. The total sits at over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the under at -115. Offensive Rankings Las Vegas : Tied for twenty-second in total offense (314.2 yards per game), 31st in rushing offense (70.7 YPG), 10th in passing offense (243.5 YPG), 10th in scoring offense (25.1 points per game). Denver : Thirtieth in total offense (277.3 yards per game), 26th in rushing offense (91.4 YPG), 25th in passing offense (185.9 YPG), 19th in scoring offense (22.0 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Just win, baby! (By starting fast offensively) The best way to put pressure on a rookie quarterback is to make the Las Vegas offense one-dimensional. Bo Nix and the Broncos offense can do their part by starting Sunday's game fast offensively and finishing drives with touchdowns. We saw glimpses of this against the Carolina Panthers, with some deep shots early by Nix, but Denver had to kick a field goal on the opening drive. Replicate that this Sunday, but finish the opening drive with a touchdown. And then do it again. And then again. Add to the pressure that the Broncos defense will undoubtedly bring on the rookie QB. — Ian St. Clair Get after Fernando Mendoza Last week, Fernando Mendoza got his first career NFL start against a fierce Seattle Seahawks defense. Prior to Mendoza being a starter, the Raiders' offensive line only allowed 11 sacks when Kirk Cousins was quarterback. Last Sunday, with the 2026 NFL Draft's top pick under center, they gave up six to the Seahawks. If Denver wants to win the game, their defensive front seven has to dominate. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph needs to throw everything he can at the rookie signal caller and rattle him early and often. — Christopher Hart Keep feeding Jonah Coleman I don't need to discuss numbers. Just look at how much better the offense is when Coleman gets his touches. Whether he's running the ball or catching passes, he gives the offense a weapon that forces the defense to respect what Denver is doing in the trenches, thus opening up the opportunities for Bo Nix to push the ball downfield. — Adam Malnati Blow a team out for once I know, I know. Buuuuut, it would sure be nice to enjoy a good ol' fashioned butt-whoopin' type game — especially against the Raiders. — Tim Lynch Score more points than the Raiders The Broncos scored more points than the Panthers a few weeks ago and didn't need to score any last week, because they were on a bye. Now, it's Raiders week, and my key to the game is simple. Score more points than the Raiders. Denver is 7-0 when it does that and 0-2 when it does not. Using advanced analytics, I say the Broncos have a 100% chance to win on Sunday if they score more points than the Raiders. away.headline: Report: Raiders TE Brock Bowers avoids major ankle injury
away.blurb: The team initially listed him as questionable to return and he came back in the second quarter with his right ankle heavily taped. He made one catch before returning to the locker room and ultimately being ruled out. Bowers, 23, finished the 21-13 defeat with two receptions for 18 yards. The third-year pro out of Georgia raised his team-leading season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Bowers is day-to-day. "It's not as bad as we thought but still a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said. Bowers, a two-time Pro Bowl selection, was hurt while blocking on a running play during the Raiders' opening drive. Multiple players rolled up on the back of his leg as he was making the block. A first-round pick (13th overall) by Las Vegas in 2024, Bowers has accumulated 226 receptions for 2,550 yards and 18 touchdowns in 37 career games (32 starts). He was a first-team All-Pro as a rookie. This story was originally published November 16, 2026 at 10:59 AM . away.headline: Will Brock Bowers play for the Raiders against the Broncos? What we know about the TE’s injury
away.blurb: The Raiders tight end returned to limited practice Thursday after missing Wednesday with ankle and quadriceps injuries. Bowers has been dealing with ankle and quadriceps injuries after leaving last Sunday’s 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. His availability remains uncertain, but his return to the practice field is a positive development for the Raiders as they prepare for a difficult divisional matchup. As of Friday morning, November 20, Bowers has not been officially ruled in or out for Sunday’s game. However, his return to practice on Thursday has improved the outlook for his availability. The tight end was listed as a limited participant in Thursday’s practice after missing Wednesday’s workout. The Raiders listed both an ankle and a quadriceps injury on their report. Kubiak also indicated that Bowers might not need to practice this week to be available against Denver. His participation on Thursday nevertheless represents an important step toward a possible return. The Raiders are scheduled to practice again Friday , when another update on Bowers’ condition is expected. The team’s final injury report should provide a clearer indication of whether he will be available against the Broncos. He caught a pass after coming back onto the field, but the ankle continued to bother him and he was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the contest. Bowers finished with two receptions for 18 yards, a significant loss for the offense, who rely heavily on his ability to create opportunities in the passing game. His potential return would be significant for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who is preparing for just his second NFL start . Bowers gives the young quarterback one of his most reliable targets against a Denver defense that has been among the league’s strongest this season. If Bowers is unavailable, Michael Mayer would be expected to take on a larger role in the Raiders’ offense. Mendoza has also highlighted the other options available to him, including wide receivers Jack Bech and Tre Tucker , as well as tight end Ian Thomas. The Raiders will hope Bowers can make enough progress to return against Denver, but his status will depend on how he responds to the remainder of the week’s practices. For now, Thursday’s limited participation is an encouraging sign . The Raiders are still waiting for confirmation that their star tight end will be ready to play on Sunday. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars-Giants: Bhayshul Tuten's Field Day Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to take on the New York Giants in one of Week 11's most interesting matchups, and there is plenty at stake for both teams. For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. Q: Why has Trevor Lawrence been so surgical against zone coverage? Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect JS: There are several reasons. He has a group of pass-catchers in Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Brenton Strange who all thrive at beating zone coverage thanks to their ability to find soft spots in zones and work the middle of the field. JS: There are several reasons. He has a group of pass-catchers in Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Brenton Strange who all thrive at beating zone coverage thanks to their ability to find soft spots in zones and work the middle of the field. Liam Coen’s scheme also gives Lawrence and the passing game plenty of open looks against zone coverage, thanks to the balance they play with on offense and how they scheme open wide receivers. But most importantly, it comes down to how Lawrence is playing. He is confident in everything he is doing before and after the snap, far more confident than he has looked in past years. He knows where the ball is going, and he knows how to fit it in there regardless of how open or tight the passing windows are. Q: How does the potential absence of center Robert Hainsey affect the offensive line? Jacksonville Jaguars center Robert Hainsey | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect JS: It will likely impact communication. The Jaguars’ offense has had some communication issues on the road this year, whether in Denver in Week 2 or in London in Weeks 5-6. JS: It will likely impact communication. The Jaguars’ offense has had some communication issues on the road this year, whether in Denver in Week 2 or in London in Weeks 5-6. That said, this might not be the crushing loss many outside Jacksonville believe it is. Hainsey has been the Jaguars’ fifth-best offensive lineman this season, and a lot of his value comes pre-snap. There is a real chance the Jaguars could see stronger play from second-year center Jonah Monheim, whom the staff rates extremely highly and who has played well in spot starts for Hainsey in the past. Q: What do you view as the key matchups, Giants offense vs. Jaguars defense and vice versa? Jacksonville Jaguars DB Travis Hunter | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect JS: When it comes to the Jaguars’ defense vs. the Giants’ offense, the biggest matchup I am going to be watching is Malik Nabers against Travis Hunter. JS: When it comes to the Jaguars’ defense vs. the Giants’ offense, the biggest matchup I am going to be watching is Malik Nabers against Travis Hunter. Hunter has been a true shutdown No. 1 cornerback this season, even beyond his amazing athletic feats on his interceptions. He is the only Jaguars cornerback who can really run with Nabers, and I am fascinated to see these two battle downfield. The Jaguars don’t have their cornerbacks following receivers, but this might be the week to consider it. As for the Jaguars’ offense vs. the Giants’ defense, I am going with Walker Little against Abdul Carter. Little has played well for the Jaguars since stepping in as the starting left tackle a month ago due to injuries, but a player on Carter’s level hasn’t tested him. Little has proven he can get the job done week in and week out, but this week will be about proving that he can handle playing a blue-chip talent, which is exactly what he will need to do during a critical playoff run. Q: What’s the most underrated part/player of the Jaguars’ overall plan of attack? Jacksonville Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect JS: Anthony Campanile. The Jaguars’ defensive coordinator is a genius, turning one of the NFL’s worst defenses into a powerhouse over the last two years. JS: Anthony Campanile. The Jaguars’ defensive coordinator is a genius, turning one of the NFL’s worst defenses into a powerhouse over the last two years. They are not flawless, since they still give up some explosive plays, and they do not get a ton of sacks. But Campanile has built one of the best run defenses in the NFL, and his philosophy of forcing quarterbacks to get the ball out of their hands quickly has led to plenty of takeaways and big plays. Campanile should be a future head coach, and the proof is in the pudding: he has helped elevate and evolve the Jaguars’ defense over the past two years. Q: The Jags have been blowing out opponents. What are your expectations for this week, though? Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect JS: I don’t think the Jaguars have a blowout this week, even though I believe they are firmly the better team. JS: I don’t think the Jaguars have a blowout this week, even though I believe they are firmly the better team. The Giants have fought hard week in and week out under John Harbaugh, and I think there is a real chance they take the fight to the Jaguars in the trenches. I think Trevor Lawrence will still be taking snaps in the fourth quarter this week, which has not been a given most weeks. There is a lot more respect in the Jaguars’ building right now than there was the last time these two teams played in 2022. picks.headline: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate
picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football MLB trade targets Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants face major test this week when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. It is also a game that will provide a huge swing in the Giants' expected chances to make the playoffs. Will the Giants upset Jacksonville? See what our Big Blue View staff members think about that game and the rest of the Week 11 action in this week's staff picks. I don't think the Giants win this game. I think there's a path to a win for the Giants, if they can find it. The Giants are one of the very best teams in the NFL at forcing drives to end in punts. At the same time, the Jaguars will be without their starting center and the Giants are one of the best teams in the League at creating quick pressure. That's important because Trevor Lawrence has been one of the quarterbacks most affected by pressure in the NFL. At the same time, the Giants have rediscovered the explosive pass with J.J. McCarthy, which has been the weakness of the Jags' defense. If the Giants can score touchdowns while disrupting Lawrence, they've got the chance to come away with the upset. We've seen the Giants rebound after bad games, as well as play much better than anticipated when they're underdogs. Maybe both will happen here. The flip side of the coin is simpler and scarier to me: The Giants have one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, and the Jaguars have one of the best red zone offenses in the league. If the Giants can't stop them between the 20s, this game could get ugly fast. Pick: Jaguars Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the league with a young and explosive offense that can run the football. Their defense is aggressive but doesn't NEED to bring the blitz — they blitz at about a league-average rate, but Anthony Campanile does an excellent job utilizing simulated pressure to harass opposing quarterbacks. Jacksonville is third in offensive EPA, 4th in defensive EPA allowed, and 1st in Net EPA — they're a juggernaut based on their performance and the advanced analytics. Still, that doesn't mean the Giants don't have a chance — they just must play efficient football and avoid the catastrophic mistakes that have robbed them of wins. It's possible, but against the most efficient team in the NFL, it will be difficult. John Harbaugh will have the Giants ready and prepared for the game, and I believe it will be more exciting and competitive. Jacksonville is concluding their third straight road game, which could give the Giants a slight advantage at home, but I ultimately believe the better team finds a way to win. David Hartman It took 11 weeks, but for the first time this season, the Giants will face a team with a winning record when the 7-2 Jaguars come to town on Sunday. Not only is Jacksonville running away with the AFC South (they lead the division by four games), but they're steamrolling the competition. They've won their last three games by a combined 75 points. This is easily Big Blue's toughest test of the season, so far. Jacksonville is very good on both sides of the ball. They're fourth in offensive DVOA, third in defensive DVOA, and third in overall DVOA. They also have an excellent field goal kicker with crazy range. If you look at both rosters, it's hard to find clear advantages for the Giants at any position group outside of tight end, and even there, Jacksonville has good players. Can the Giants win this game? Yes. They're at home, they're getting an extra three days of rest, and as we saw when they played Houston, they aren't scared and can surprise as a big underdog. They'll need to dial it up on defense and pressure Trevor Lawrence into the kinds of mistakes he used to make before Liam Coen got there. They also might have a little extra motivation after letting last week's game against the Commanders slip away at the end. I won't be surprised if John Harbaugh's team hangs in there and keeps it as a one-score game most of the way. But in the end, until the Giants show me that they can beat a really good team, I can't pick them to do so. Tony Del Genio You can talk yourself into believing that the Giants can beat Jacksonville this Sunday. They needed a miraculous last-second 57-yard field goal to beat the Eagles team (with Jalen Hurts) that the Giants defeated (without Hurts). They lost to the Texans team that the Giants beat the following week. The woeful Titans were within a TD against them last week with 5 minutes left. So indeed, it could be a competitive game. Unfortunately, the Jags have also won games by 24, 29, 35, and 23 points this season. They have scored 31 or more in each of their past four games, and over 40 in two of those. The Giants have only scored more than 30 points once, and only then because of a 99-yard pick-6 on the last play of the game. Trevor Lawrence isn't necessarily playing any better this year than in the past. He's a QB that simultaneously makes great passes and puts the ball up for grabs, yet unlike in years past, he's cut down on the INTs while getting the TDs. Part of that may be due to 5'10" wide receiver Parker Washington (a 2023 6th-round pick), who had a breakout 2025 and is on pace for 1,000 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, a 4th round 2025 pick, isn't quite in the Jahmyr Gibbs – Kenneth Walker class but he's not far below and is a missed tackle machine. A lot of the credit has to go to head coach Liam Coen, who also calls the plays and turned this team around as soon as he was hired. Lawrence, like most QBs, has trouble with pressure, but he is not too fazed by the blitz. Finding a way to disrupt his rhythm is a key to any chance the Giants may have. On defense, the Jaguars are strong at linebacker with fourth-round 2023 pick Ventrell Miller, one of the league's best (note how many mid-round picks the Jags have hit on), along with Foyesade Oluokun. They also put on a decent pass rush with Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and Dennis Gardeck. In the secondary, Travis Hunter is playing more like a No. 2 pick, having mostly given up his evening gig as a receiver. Are the Giants a serious playoff contender? This is the type of game they can use to make a statement against a team that is in the Super Bowl conversation. I think they'll put up a fight. I also don't think they're there yet. Pick : Jaguars Valentine's View I want to convince myself to pick the Giants to defeat the Jaguars. I really do. I just can't. The Jaguars are a team with justifiable Super Bowl ambitions . They are a well-rounded team with a high-powered offense, a very good defense, and one of the best field-goal kickers in the business in Cam Little. The Giants are a good team. They are resilient. They will give the Jaguars their best shot. Maybe, just maybe, it will be good enough to pull off an upset that would go a long way toward ensuring that the Giants make the playoffs. I just can't pick them to do it.

TV: CBS (Jim Nantz, J.J. Watt, Tracy Wolfson). Radio: 1010-XL/92.5-FM (Frank Frangie, Jeff Lageman, Bucky Brooks); Spanish, 106.7-FM (Javier Carrero, Victor Cora); Sirius XM Channel 814. Records: Jaguars 7-2, Giants 5-3-1. Jacksonville Jaguars running back Travis Etienne Jr. (1) celebrates his first quarter touchdown with quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) during a game against the New York Giants at EverBank Field in on Oct. 23, 2022. What happened last week? The Jaguars beat the Tennessee Titans 40-23 in Nashville. The Giants lost to Washington 24-21. What are the Jaguars-Giants odds? The Jaguars are 6-point favorites, according to BetMGM . They're -275 on the money line. The Giants are +225. The over-under is 46.5 points. Who's injured? Jaguars: Out — C Robert Hainsey (knee), DE B.J. Green (forearm). Questionable — DT Matt Dickerson (neck), DE Danny Striggow (concussion). Giants: The Giants are not reporting any players out or questionable. What's the series history between the Jaguars and Giants? The two teams are tied 4-4. New York is 3-1 vs. the Jaguars at home. The last time the Jaguars played the Giants at MetLife Stadium was in 2018, when they won 20-15 . The last time the Jaguars played at MetLife Stadium was on Dec. 22, 2022, when they beat the New York Jets 19-3 . What happened the last time the Jaguars played the Giants? Christian Kirk was tackled just short of the goal line and the Giants won 23-17 on Oct. 23, 2022, in Jacksonville. Trevor Lawrence threw for 310 yards and Kirk caught seven passes for 96 yards. What's the key Jaguars-Giants matchup? Jaguars DT Jordan Davis vs. Giants RB Cam Skattebo With a chance of rain on Sunday in East Rutherford, the game might turn into a low-scoring battle, with running the ball and the ability to stop the run the key to winning. Expect a few collisions between Skattebo, the Giants' leading rusher (496 yards, 4.3 per carry) and Davis, the Jaguars' acquisition from Philadelphia two weeks ago who will be playing his first game for the Jags. J.J. McCarthy (18) of the New York Giants is sacked by Jordan Davis of the Philadelphia Eagles during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on Nov. 8, 2026 in Philadelphia. Davis will be playing his second game in a row against the Giants. His last game as an Eagle was a 19-11 loss to New York on Nov. 8, but he played well, with two tackles for losses and a sack. Skattebo was injured and did not play in that game, but last week he had 78 yards rushing and two touchdowns and three receptions for 44 yards in the loss to Washington. What's notable about Jaguars vs. Giants? The Jaguars are playing their third straight road game, which has happened six times in franchise history. The Jaguars are 5-1 in those games, with four of the five victories coming in playoff seasons. ... The Jaguars won the first two games, at Baltimore and Tennessee. They've swept three-game road trips twice, in 2001 and 2005. ... This will be the sixth time in eight weeks that the Jaguars have played away from Jacksonville, counting the two London games. ... If the Jaguars win, they will be 10-3 on the road under coach Liam Coen . The only NFL coaches to win 10 or more road games in fewer games over the past 25 years are Mike Macdonald and Sean McVay with 11 each. ... Lawrence has set a franchise record with seven consecutive games of a 95.0 or better passer rating. It's also the longest current active streak in the NFL. ... The Jaguars are 5-9 overall in East Rutherford against both the Giants and the Jets. picks.headline: Experts Giving Giants Low Chance to Defeat Jaguars This Week
picks.blurb: Experts Giving Giants Low Chance to Defeat Jaguars This Week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football MLB trade targets Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended Experts Giving Giants Low Chance to Defeat Jaguars This Week (Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 8:41 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants will finally be getting back on the field this week, following a long absence after a loss on Thursday Night Football in Week 10. But as the Giants prepare for the upcoming game, this could be a real challenge for the team to deal with. New York will be hosting the Jacksonville Jaguars this week, giving the team a true test to overcome. For the year, the Giants hold a record of 5-3-1, sitting in first place of the NFC East, at least for now. New York has been trying to get back to the playoffs, and this game against Jacksonville could help out greatly. As for the Jaguars, they will enter the game with a record of 7-2 for the season, sitting in first place of the AFC South. Jacksonville is among the top teams in the NFL, and they may be the most well-rounded roster in the league. But the Giants will try to pull off the upset at home, and New York has been very good playing at MetLife this year. New York is 3-2 at home this season, giving them a slight edge entering the contest with Jacksonville. Experts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report made game picks for all matchups in Week 11. Within these, only two of the seven picked the Giants to grab the victory at home over the Jaguars. Only Gagnon and Hanford went with the Giants to get the win, which speaks to the level of trust in the team. But Jacksonville is one of the stronger teams in the NFL, and this could be a tough matchup for New York. The big key in this game will be the play from quarterback J.J. McCarthy against a tough Jaguars defense. McCarthy will look to bounce back from a costly turnover in the team's last game, but that could be easier said than done. So far this season, McCarthy has thrown for 915 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. The former first-round draft pick has helped spark new life into the Giants' offense, but the team needs more from him going forward. For New York to take down the Jaguars, McCarthy will need to push the ball down the field, keeping up with the scoring. Jacksonville has been a lethal offense, and the Giants can't afford to settle for field goals or turnovers.

away.headline: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus
away.blurb: The Jaguars had 11 players carry either a limited or did-not-participate designation into Thursday's practice. Some names, like center Robert Hainsey's DNP situation due to a knee injury, were expected. But there was one change to Thursday's injury report that will trump all other names: Bhayshul Tuten, who was downgraded to a non-participant in practice after practicing in a limited fashion on Wednesday, which now creates quite the injury development to monitor before the Jaguars play the New York Giants in Week 11 on Sunday afternoon. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen has said in recent days that he has been pleased with Tuten's performances and toughness over the last two weeks. Add this to the fact that he played the last few weeks without a full week of practice, and it is hard to imagine Tuten sitting this one out, even if his injury will now come even more into focus. The Jaguars also had the following players listed as limited on Thursday: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- We are at that point of the season where injury reports closer resemble CVS receipts, and the Jaguars' Thursday injury report certainly checks that box. Tuten's status is a key one to watch any week, but especially in Week 11 when the Jaguars' running game is supposed to be pivotal against a blitz-happy Giants front that will test the Jaguars in the trenches. Tuten has played in each of the last two games despite practicing just once in those two weeks, and the Jaguars clearly did not feel like Tuten couldn't handle the bulk of the carries when he got 26 carries against the Titans on Sunday. “Obviously, last year being in a supplemental role, and I thought he was tough last year in some of the runs that he had where he just would kind of get whacked pretty good, get up and continue to play," Coen said on Wednesday. "To carry the load that he took this past week with 26 carries and play the amount of snaps he played still not quite 100%. I think the guy is probably mentally and physically tougher than I would've maybe imagined in ways." The smart bet would be to prepare for Tuten to play, but that does not mean this will not be a situation to monitor. It is such a key injury to watch in large part because the Jaguars have leaned on Tuten significantly over the course of the season. The second-year running back is arguably one of the three most important players on the offense alongside Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington, and he has vastly outproduced the rest of the Jaguars' running back room. This is a big one, just like each game is a big one. But unless something changes on Friday, Tuten still should be considered a key part of Sunday's game. home.headline: Giants Cam Skattebo Reveals Backflip Celebration's Future After Aidan Hutchinson's Knee Injury
home.blurb: Cam Skattebo is retiring the backflip. The New York Giants' running back said he will no longer do his signature celebration after seeing Detroit Lions' pass-rusher Aidan Hutchinson tear his ACL during a sack celebration on Sunday. "It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters Monday. "I'm saying yeah [no more backflips]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.' That ain't going to happen to me." He did add that he might bring back the backflip "if we go to the playoffs or something," but acknowledged that Hutchinson "didn't think about [the risk] either, and it happened." You have to think folks with the Giants' organization were jumping for joy—backflipping for joy, even—after hearing Skattebo's comments on the matter.
